text:
scan-bot: Automated leak scanner (ci-leak-scan) flagged a match in build #4823. File: tests/fixtures/ci_creds.json, pattern: 'private_key_id'. Possible GCP service account JSON committed in test fixtures. Artifact link: https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-ci/builds/4823/artifacts/ci_creds.json

maya: saw this. is that a real SA key or a placeholder? where did the fixture come from?

samir: it looks real — private_key and client_email are populated. repo path is infra/experiment-tests/tests/fixtures. CI caches artifacts into GCS; that cache is what the scanner picked up.

alex: containment first: disable the SA and revoke that key id, block CI from restoring the cache for that repo. also capture audit logs (IAM & KMS) to see if key was used.

maya: i'll open an incident ticket ENGSEC-621 and start rotation. can someone confirm key id from the file? scanner shows `abcd1234` as the private_key_id.

samir: quick snippets i ran locally:
```
$ gitleaks detect --source=./infra/experiment-tests --report-format=json | jq '.matches[] | {file: .filename, rule: .rule, entropy: .entropy}'
{"file":"tests/fixtures/ci_creds.json","rule":"gcp-service-account","entropy":7.3}
```
and a targeted grep: `git grep -n "private_key_id" -- infra/ || true` returned the single hit above.

alex: i'm revoking CI cache access to `gs://redwood-ci-cache/experiment-tests/*` right now and will patch the workflow to not restore that key. also posting an ops ACL change to block that path for the build service account.

maya: rotation actions: disabled the service account at 2024-11-06T14:12Z, revoked key `abcd1234`. Updated ENGSEC-621 with timestamps and GCP console links. Added audit snapshot (IAM admin audit logs) to the ticket.

samir: next manual steps: remove the committed file from repo history and replace with a fixture generator. proposed commands:
```
# remove file from history (example)
git filter-repo --path infra/experiment-tests/tests/fixtures/ci_creds.json --invert-paths
```
we'll land that in a new branch and coordinate with release train so nobody is surprised.

maya: long-term remediation: switch test harness to use workload identity or short-lived tokens instead of checked-in keys. enforce pre-commit gitleaks and add a check in CI that rejects artifacts with `private_key` before caching. also add a PR checklist item about test fixtures.

alex: i'll coordinate with infra (cc @infra) to add a temporary deny rule on the GCS bucket and update the CI templates to read secrets via KMS or OIDC. we should also run a retro scan across all repos for the last 5 years and surface any other hits.

security-bot: Created ENGSEC-621: "revoked-SA-key-found-in-test-fixture". Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2024-11-08 16:00 PT.

maya: thanks. i've attached the revoked key id, audit log export, and remediation checklist to the ticket. tagging compliance for export.

samir: i'll open a PR to remove the fixture and add the generator. will also add `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with gitleaks rules.

alex: owners: maya = incident lead & audit export, samir = repo cleanup PR, infra = CI cache/block and KMS rollout. i'll follow up with a short incident summary for execs after the postmortem.

maya: :thumbsup: closing the immediate containment. anyone who sees related hits, paste them here and i'll triage. we'll track follow-ups in ENGSEC-621 and the repo cleanup PR.
